items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: And so Ray Brown came to the gig to hear us. And Ray had been at the school with Oscar when I studied there. So he said, “Man, Dizzy’s not going to teach you cats like he did us in the 40s,”

ctx.x: Dizzy became Baha’i five years before I did, but I had been studying it. I had an experience at the Jazz Workshop in Boston where I read it’s called the Long Healing Prayer. I awoke in the middle of the night in a panic man. I was like — anxiety. And I called this lady, Nancy Jordan, who was a Baha’i and her husband, Jordan, he was on the faculty at Yale or something, in the psychology department. She came to Boston and she had a pamphlet that talked about when you shed your old self and your real self comes out…
